## Outline

- (30m) Tool calling
  - Demo [`_demos/15_demo_manual-tools`](https://github.com/posit-conf-2026/llms/tree/main/_demos/15_demo_manual-tools): a human relays tool calls between the LLM and the functions
  - Demo [`_demos/16_demo_tools`](https://github.com/posit-conf-2026/llms/tree/main/_demos/16_demo_tools): the same tools, registered with ellmer or chatlas
  - Your Turn [`_exercises/17_quiz-game-2`](https://github.com/posit-conf-2026/llms/tree/main/_exercises/17_quiz-game-2): register a `play_sound` tool (`beepr` in R, [playsound](https://pypi.org/project/playsound3/) in Python) in the Quiz Show app
  - Your Turn [`_exercises/18_quiz-game-3`](https://github.com/posit-conf-2026/llms/tree/main/_exercises/18_quiz-game-3): add tool annotations to give the tool a title and an icon. The exercise points to `ContentToolResult` if you want richer tool displays.

## Further reading

Hadley Wickham's "What is an agent?" series on Substack explains tools, harnesses, and agents from first principles with ellmer examples:

- [What is an agent?](https://tidydesign.substack.com/p/what-is-an-agent) — conversations, turns, rounds, tools, and a precise definition of an agent.
- [Your LLM can't math (and that's ok)](https://tidydesign.substack.com/p/your-llm-cant-math-and-thats-ok) — how tool calls actually work, and why web chats can do things a bare LLM can't.
